newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks pare losses at close, rescue news aids.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks pare losses at close, rescue news aids.

text.p: Thai stocks, which tumbled early on Friday, pared losses by the close after news that a private sector rescue fund would shore up the market, brokers said.

The SET index, which fell for the seventh consecutive trading day, finished down 1.48 percent or 15.17 points at 1,007.51 on 6.8 billion baht trade. Decliners led gainers 335 to 51 while 86 issues were unchanged. The SET-50 index fell 0.98 point to 76.46.
"The report on the injection of private rescue funds to assist the bourse has helped boost market sentiment," said a broker.
The SET index finished at a 35-month-low, the lowest level since it closed at 998.71 in October 1994.

During the session, the index fell to an intraday low at 988.03 but climbed back after the Thai Bankers' Association late on friday the fund would move into the market and state-owned Krung Thai Bank confirmed it could advance funds to do so.
Banks and brokers contribute to the 5.0 billion baht fund.
Brokers also agred to chip in to the fund.
However, investors were still wary of lingering rumours that some brokerages were hit by some indebted investors unable to meet their margin loan obligations, brokers said.
The rumour prompted brokerages to force sell stocks held by financially weak players, mainly locals, brokers said.

"Moody's decision to downgrade Thailand's short-term debt ratings earlier this week is another concern which keeps investors jittery," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of Sitca Investment and Securities.

The energy sector was the only one to survive Friday's fall, rising 1.41 percent, while others fell heavily. Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 165. Finance One retreated 2.50 to 94.50 and Advanced Info Service dropped six to 300. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 252-9950
